03-World-Area-Field/Weather/weather-probability-and-transition-roll.md - "One function, two names"

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Script-Object-Accessors/phyre-script-object-accessors.md - the GFZ CodeDomain tag and the bound type name the SAME accessor at different granularity; section 8 measures the tag against string evidence at 100% precision (0 GFZ-only), so a tagged address is always the accessor the string names. The Lua bindings doc lists this address as an ObjectPointerAccessor sample; this doc gives the type it binds.

00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Object-Model/vtable-method-index.md - NOT the same name: 23-Third-Party-Libraries lists this as a 'lua_pcall CALL SITE' and marks it 'not read', so the matched token is the CALLEE's name, not this address's. The index gives its owning class (PCallerScript slot 2). Recorded here because the checker cannot tell a callee column from a name column. NOTE: a direct-call check finds 0 of this function's 59 calls going to any Lua-tagged function, so the call-site claim remains unverified.

00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Object-Model/vtable-method-index.md - complementary, not conflicting: the GFZ already names this function SteamController_PollState and the index adds that it is slot 5 of Phyre's PInputDevicePadSteamController vtable. One is what the function does, the other is the class whose slot it occupies; together they show Phyre's Steam pad device class is what drives Steam controller polling.

01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/Verb-Dispatch/scriptvm-verb-dispatch-and-parameter-encoding.md - the GFZ name is WRONG, not merely coarse: the function returns a float in xmm0 on all four exit paths and callers consume it, so it discards nothing. It is the pop-as-float32 counterpart to 00267E10's pop-as-int. Recorded rather than renamed because the sanctioned pipeline has NO rename script - the only writers are ApplyCurrentBodyCodeDomainBatch{,AllowExisting}, which write CodeDomain tags - and renaming through the Ghidra GUI would mutate outside the gate and invalidate the snapshot hash. Database documents use name_b; name_a is retained only to trace back to the annotation set.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Animation-Channel-Binding/animation-channel-binding-and-transform-composition.md - complementary, not conflicting. name_a is the RTTI class whose vtable slot this address occupies (from the unique-class subset of the recovered index); name_b is what the body does, argued from the complete body plus its own authored string "Not binding %s:%s because array index (%d) exceeds array size (%d)". Class membership and behaviour are different facts about one function.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Animation-Channel-Binding/animation-channel-binding-and-transform-composition.md - complementary. name_a is the class, name_b is slot 9's behaviour read from the complete body: mark[slot[i]]=1 for every input, with slot 0 marked UNCONDITIONALLY regardless of weight - the one write that distinguishes additive from weighted blending.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Animation-Channel-Binding/animation-channel-binding-and-transform-composition.md - complementary. Same slot, same class-vs-behaviour split as 005C6020; this one marks only where weight != 0.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Animation-Channel-Binding/animation-channel-binding-and-transform-composition.md - complementary. name_a is the class; name_b is slot 12's behaviour: classify each channel by semantic pointer identity, group by target, compose the TRS matrix. NOTE the slot number is NOT a shared interface - PAnimationBlenderController's slot 12 (005C9F30) is an array resize, an unrelated function.

23-Third-Party-Libraries/Bullet-Physics-Integration/phyre-to-bullet-rigid-body-materialization.md - the same reading at two lengths. name_a is the GFZ CodeDomain tag (truncated to 60 chars by the consistency checker's name column); name_b is the short working name this database uses for the same function. No disagreement of substance - both say it builds a btCompoundShape and a btRigidBody out of a Phyre rigid-body description.

23-Third-Party-Libraries/Bullet-Physics-Integration/phyre-to-bullet-rigid-body-materialization.md - the same name with and without its CodeDomain namespace prefix; the checker truncates name_a at 60 chars, which is what makes them look different. Body not fully read - see BN-3.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/member-registration-and-the-recovered-field-schema.md - complementary, not conflicting. name_a is the GFZ CodeDomain tag naming the mechanism family; name_b is the recovered signature argued from the complete body: PClassDataMember_Register(record, owner, PType *memberType, name, offset, attrs, flag2, ctx). The tag was right about what the function is FOR; it does not state the signature, and the signature is what the 682-row schema rests on.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/member-registration-and-the-recovered-field-schema.md - complementary. name_a is a broad CodeDomain family label; name_b is the specific constructor, identified by its store of the attribute word to record +0x28 - the same byte the class-descriptor document's teardown helper tests before freeing the name string, derived independently from the opposite end.

22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/member-registration-and-the-recovered-field-schema.md - complementary. name_a names the registry; name_b names this function's role within it. Body evidence: ordered-tree walk on the h*0x21 + (c & 0x1F) hash, falling through to a byte-by-byte string compare when two hashes are equal, so the hash is an ordering key and never an identity (BK-9).

24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Exception-Handling-And-Unwind/exception-funclets-and-lazy-static-guards.md and 18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/how-a-sound-request-becomes-a-voice.md - NOT a disagreement: this is an /OPT:ICF FOLD. The address is a 3-byte "ret 0" that the linker merged ~273 identically-bodied functions onto, and it has 2,479 distinct callers across 2,867 call sites, with 2,511 functions referencing it at all (1,515 of those through data pointer slots). RECONCILED 2026-09-02; an earlier 2,480 was not reproducible under any definition. The CFG check named in the load config, a retail-stripped assert, and 172 folded empty destructors are all genuinely this address; the binary does not record which original each caller meant. Open question BA-1. Treat any claim about "what 0016D6A0 does" as a claim about one caller's intent, never about the address. Also load-bearing elsewhere: BQ-27 records that 1,606 deleting destructors route their sized-delete branch here and therefore free nothing.

00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Object-Model/vtable-method-index.md and 18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/how-a-sound-request-becomes-a-voice.md - a folded or shared address with two independent readings: name_a is the RTTI class whose vtable slot it occupies, name_b is a behavioural reading of the body (a 4-byte field getter at +0x24). The body is a single field load, which is exactly the shape /OPT:ICF folds across unrelated classes, so both may name real original functions. NOTE this address ALSO carries a GFZ ownership retraction that its tags do not reflect - see BR-1, one of exactly seven such functions - so it should not be counted toward Audio ownership by any census.

18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/ - the SAME reading at two confidence levels, kept deliberately rather than reconciled. The body reads DAT_0215EF44; a whole-image xref census over that global shows eight writers whose bodies make it a single current-track slot (002DECE0 swaps it after stopping the old, 002DEDE0 clears it to -1 on a match, two others substitute it when the caller passes negative), so "current track handle" is body-proven and -1 is its empty value. The "Music" prefix rests on ONE FURTHER INFERENCE - that MusicAudioBank is the one bank class the play call cannot reach - which is strong but unproven. name_a is the form with no inference in it and is what this database's conservative documents use.

18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/ - same split as 002DEC00. "Level" is solid: the value written to 0215EF4D is a 0-127 level, three separate writers set it to the literal 0x7F, its only reader in the image is 002DE350, and 002DECE0 sets 0x7F then immediately calls 001DBC70(track, 0x7F) - the same numeric domain as the play call's volume. The "Music" prefix carries the same single unproven inference as above. Both names describe one function; they differ only in how far the author was willing to push it.

00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Shared-State-Accessors/cross-subsystem-accessor-hubs.md Hub 4, and the body: 0031B776 cmp cl,0x27 / ja bounds the input to 0..39, 0031B77B resolves 02EBF190 and 0031B789 imul rcx,rax,0x1c8 forms *(02EBF190)+8+i*0x1C8, then 0031B7B1 cmp qword ptr [rax+0x698], rdi scans live units for the one whose stats record IS that element. NOT A RENAME - functions.tsv is a shared generated artifact and is not hand-edited. The second name is recorded because the first misleads in a way that costs a caller: 'combatant id' reads as any combatant, and THIS FUNCTION CANNOT REACH A KIND-1 (SpawnKeep-backed) UNIT AT ALL, by construction - a kind-1 unit's +0x698 is SpawnKeep entry + 0x80 (0023A787 sub rax,-0x80; stored 0023ABFA), which is never an element of the 02EBF190 array the scan compares against. Calling it for an enemy returns 0, and the name does not say so.

00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Shared-State-Accessors/cross-subsystem-accessor-hubs.md Hub 4, and the whole 33-byte body: 00320A40 cmp cl,0x27 / jbe bounds the input to 0..39, 00320A4B imul rcx,rax,0x1c8, 00320A52 mov rax,[rip+0x2b9e737] resolving to 02EBF190, then add 8 and add rcx - byte for byte the expression BattleUnit_ApplyUnitDefinition uses on its kind-0 arm. 'battle slot' suggests any battle participant; the bound is 40 PARTY slots and the same kind-1 unreachability applies. Recorded, not renamed, for the same reason as 0031B770.
